Subscription.description: What a subscriber is told of: events of the kinds listed, narrowed to the queues, scope and items named, an empty list or a null scope matching all. With a url each event is posted there as the subscription-event webhook; without one it is read on GET /events with subscriptionId. A subscription with ttlMs runs out at expiresAt unless a change renews it. A webhook that keeps failing moves it to failing, where it is still tried every five minutes and moved back to active by the first post taken; setting state back to active delivers again at once from the event after deliveredEventId.

info.description: A todo kept as middleware: items, notes, reports, work orders and their tasks, queues, leases on items, questions and their replies, and subscriptions, stored and served through this API and nothing else. The service never executes: it launches no run and calls no other service; the only calls it makes are deliveries to the addresses its subscribers registered. Work reaches whoever does it two ways, side by side: pushed, as the events of a subscription it registered, and pulled, by a lease. Who a member belongs to is opaque to the service: scope and the <role>Name fields are the caller's strings, and labels the caller's metadata.

post.description: Posted to the url the subscriber registered, with the subscription's key in the Job-Subscription header and, where a secret was given, sha256= and the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body under it in Job-Signature. A 2xx acknowledges it within a minute; anything else is tried again with backoff, ten failures in a row move the subscription to failing, and a failing one is tried every five minutes until a post is taken. The subscriber drops an event it has seen by its id.

x-harness.entry: A harness subscribes with job_subscribe to the queues it serves (or names them when it starts the server), and is told of each item opened there by an MCP notification; it takes that item, or the next of a queue, with job_lease_next, reads its brief, notes and work order, hears words appended while it works by the same subscription or job_notes, reports with job_report and closes the item. The server renews the leases and subscriptions it took while its harness runs, and lets them go when it stops.
x-harness.notifications: The MCP server reads its subscriptions in the stream form and sends each event as an MCP notification: notifications/resources/updated on the resource job://items/{itemId} or job://queues/{queueName} the event names, and, where it was started with a channel, the event itself as notifications/<channel> carrying content and meta, for a harness that takes messages pushed into its session.

input.description: A route's path key and the rest of its input together, as one tool's input.

after.description: The key of the last member read; the page continues past it.

limit.description: How many members at most, 50 where left out and at most 500.

waitMs.description: How long to hold the answer open where nothing stands past the cursor, at most 60000.

x-tools.name: job_replies

x-tools.description: Reply to a question: settle it with a choice or an answer, or add a word that settles nothing. A question put to the supervisor is settled only under a caller the deployment marks as supervising the work.

input.description: A route's path key and the rest of its input together, as one tool's input.

settles.description:
Whether the reply settles the question; left out, it settles where it carries a choice or the question
has none.

x-tools.name: job_reply

x-tools.description: Change a question while it waits: its state, its words, choices and recommendation; with addressee person, put a question the supervisor holds to a person, in your own words, with two choices or more and a recommendation, in the same change, and waitMs for how long the person has, held to the deployment's question wait, a minute unless its settings name another, which also stands where left out, after which the recommendation settles it; with addressee supervisor, take a question put to a person back while nobody has settled it. Only a caller the deployment marks as supervising the work moves the addressee.

input.description: A route's path key and the rest of its input together, as one tool's input.

addressee.description:
`person` puts a question the supervisor holds to a person, and `supervisor` takes one put to a person back
while nobody has settled it; only a supervising caller may.

heardThrough.description: The last reply the asker was handed.

ifAddressee.description:
Makes the whole change conditional on the question being put to this addressee; nothing is changed and the
change is refused `conflict` otherwise.

toldAs.description: The asker's reference to the notice it put the question before whoever answers it with, set or replaced.

waitMs.description:
With `addressee` `person` alone: how long the person has before its due time passes, 1 000 to 86 400 000
milliseconds from the move, held to the deployment's question wait, a minute unless its settings name another,
which also stands where this is left out. Its recommendation settles it then.

x-tools.name: job_question_change

x-tools.description: Subscribe to be told of work: the event kinds, queues, scope and items to hear of, a url for webhook delivery or none to be told in this session as MCP notifications, and ttlMs. The server renews it while the session lasts and deletes it when the session ends.

input.description: A subscription made.

itemIds.description: Items to hear of; empty for every item.

kinds.description: Event kinds to hear of; empty for every kind.

queueNames.description: Queues to hear of; empty for every queue.

secret.description: The key the webhook's body is signed with.

ttlMs.description: The span, 1000 to 86400000; left out, the subscription stands until it is deleted.

url.description:
An absolute http or https address to post each event to; left out, the subscription is read as a
stream.
